To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
chordoma is a rare cancer that can be successfully targeted through a combination of molecular and clinical approaches, which can be applied to any orphan cancer.
chordoma is characterized by the presence of T and EGFR amplifications and that these genetic alterations are associated with increased cell proliferation.

1) T is a bona fide oncogene in chordoma; 2) EGFR overexpression is a hallmark of chordoma; 3) T and EGFR cooperate in promoting cell proliferation; 4) the inhibition of EGFR signaling impairs the T-induced proliferative effect; 5) the inhibition of T signaling is effective in chordoma.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the genetic events that are involved in the molecular oncogenesis of chordoma and the evaluation of their potential role in promoting tumor progression.
the development of new paradigms for the molecular targeting of orphan cancers, such as chordoma.
the development of novel therapeutic strategies for the treatment of rare cancers, such as chordoma, in which the molecular pathogenesis is still largely unknown.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the molecular pathogenesis is unveiled, a new paradigm for the molecular targeting of rare sarcomas is established, and the preclinical rationale for clinical testing is provided.
the molecular pathogenesis and the preclinical rationale of chordoma have finally been unveiled, paving the way to a novel paradigm of molecular targeted treatment for this rare cancer.
the inhibition of brachyury and/or EGFR is a credible and promising therapeutic strategy in chordoma, and should be tested in a clinical trial.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the molecular pathogenesis has finally been unveiled, and the way is paved for a rational therapeutic targeting.
, for chordoma, we have now the opportunity to start a rational clinical trial based on the inhibition of EGFR and/or T, with the aim of improving the outcome of this devastating disease.
the pathogenesis of chordomas is not as rare as previously thought, and that it is not so different from that of other epithelial cancers.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, by using an integrative genomics approach, we have been able to unveil the molecular pathogenesis underlying chordoma, a cancer that was previously thought to be driven by genetic alterations of the Hedgehog pathway.
chordoma is an orphan cancer with a molecular pathogenesis that is amenable to molecularly targeted therapy.
chordoma represents an ideal model for the development of innovative therapeutic strategies, which can be easily translated to other rare cancers.
